correctness.rationale: A minimal zero forcing set represents exactly \(k-1\) legs. Before the center turns blue, each represented leg must use one of the three inclusion-minimal path seeds: an eligible root singleton, a leaf singleton, or an adjacent nonleaf pair. Trigger necessity and the shallow-pair redundancy rule give the noncentered classification; center-containing minimal sets force precisely the stated root pattern. Maximizing the number of doubled deep-pair legs and comparing with the centered extra vertex yields the formula. An independent brute-force reconstruction over 281 spider profiles of order at most 10 matched every minimal set and the upper formula exactly; this finite check only corroborates the symbolic proof.
